title: DICTO: Collected Geometric Works
description:
DICTO is a geometric sculptor in Osaka. The work grows out of building with recycled PET bottles and from three open apps on one shared geometry: Kaleidohedra, Rhombiverse and Polyhedraverse.

This record gathers all of DICTO's published geometry in one place. It opens with a short essay, Quanta of Space, which reads the works as a study of the pieces from which space is built, from the atoms of the ancients (Democritus, Plato's Timaeus) to the quanta of modern physics (loop quantum gravity), and as a bridge between periodic and aperiodic order. The papers follow in four chapters: Atoms (new solids), Bonds (how pieces fill space), Shells (layers round a core) and Cycles (rules that turn one shell into the next). Each paper has its own DICTO DOI, which always opens its newest version; the numbers (#1, #2 …) are the paper numbers on dictospheres.com; DICTO's findings are numbered separately, F1, F2 ….

Version 39 (28 October 2026) adds #69, The Hexagonality Law and the Fibonacci Stacking, and gives DICTO's ORCID iD 0009-0001-2620-2036. Version 38 (28 October 2026) adds #68, Real Polytypes and the Hexagonality Law. Version 37 (28 October 2026) adds #67, Random Stackings and Stacking Faults: the Hexagonality Law at Work. Version 36 (28 October 2026) adds #66, The Focus: One Study of Space in Pieces, and the Hexagonality Law, and lists Version 3 of #63 and Version 2 of #65 (direction vectors, exact checks, tables of every slice pattern, and Alicia Boole Stott's 1900 paper, now read). Version 35 (28 October 2026) adds #64, The Swap Rule in Crystals: Rock Salt, Cadmium Iodide, Zinc Blende and the Laves Phases on Every Stacking, and #65, The Red Queen 120-cell: Aristotle's five pyramids as the cores of the regular four-dimensional solids; section 3 of the introduction, until now Aristotle's mistake, is now Aristotle's pyramids (Aristotle wrote “the pyramid” without saying which; only the later reading of it as the regular tetrahedron fails, and #44, #63 and #65 carry his claim into four dimensions); section 5 gains a note on the rule of halves and the Swap Rule. Version 34 (28 October 2026) lists Version 2 of #63, The White Queen 600-cell (the fifteen Cleo shells read the same backwards), and Version 4 of the data set DICTO Solids: Exact Geometry (Ganesha D84, Humpty Dumpty D85, Shadow-17 D86). Version 33 (27 October 2026) added #62, Shadows of the Fourth Dimension, and #63, The White Queen 600-cell, and a paragraph on the history of the shells (Aristotle, Bradwardine, Kepler, the 600-cell). Version 32 (27 October 2026) added #61, The Swap Rule: Ganesha, the Janus Tetrahedra of Squashed Stackings, and the Border at True Close Packing. Version 31 (27 October 2026) added #60, DICTO Janus c/h Pyrochlore; #59 is now at version 2 (a corrected volume). Version 28 (25 October 2026) adds #56, Sonsam and Lahdeli: the Delian Bond on the Twinned Octet, with Ian Dury, Blockhead and Keyed Switch Points, and lists the solids named in the Bonds papers under Atoms. Version 27 (25 October 2026) adds #54, One Turn Is a Gnomon: the Golden Cycle Step by Step, and the Polar of the Keyed Pair. Version 26 (25 October 2026) adds #55, David and Goliath: Jessen's Icosahedron and the Tetrahedron in the A15 Weight Walk. Version 25 (25 October 2026) adds #53, The Global Web of Bonds: How Bonds Hand Over Across Crystal Networks. Version 24 (25 October 2026) adds #52, The Web of Bonds: How the DICTONIC Bonds Hand Over; lists the newest papers first, with a What's new box on the first page; names the six DICTONIC SOLIDS and three DICTONIC BONDS in the introduction; and lists the DICTONIC world and the data set DICTO Solids: Exact Geometry (DICTO DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23606967). Version 23 (24 October 2026) added #50, One Move Each.
